ENGN.01.note: IMAX's official overview explains the integrated system of large-format capture, projection, sound, screen geometry, and theatre design rather than treating IMAX as only a screen size.

exercise.prompt: Compare standard cinema and IMAX by capture format, image area, projection, aspect ratio, screen geometry, seating field of view, and sound system.

ENGN.02.note: Formula 1's technical explainer uses a current race car to connect wing profiles, pressure differences, ground effect, downforce, drag, and setup compromises.

article.title: F1 EXPLAINS: Downforce and why F1 cars have wings — with McLaren aero specialist Emel Cankaya

exercise.prompt: Draw the aerodynamic forces on an F1 car and explain how increasing wing angle changes cornering grip, tyre load, drag, top speed, and energy use.

ENGN.03.note: The Bluetooth SIG overview introduces the radio, protocol stack, topology, Classic and Low Energy modes, frequency use, and interoperability ecosystem.

exercise.prompt: Trace a Bluetooth Low Energy connection from advertising and scanning through connection, service discovery, characteristic access, and disconnection.

ENGN.04.note: Intel's manufacturing overview follows processor fabrication from purified silicon and wafers through repeated deposition, lithography, etching, doping, interconnect, testing, cutting, and packaging.

exercise.prompt: Create a process flow from silicon ingot to packaged CPU and mark which stages add material, remove material, change electrical properties, or inspect defects.

ENGN.05.note: D23's animation glossary entry explains the transparent celluloid layer that allowed moving characters to be painted separately from reusable backgrounds.

article.title: Cel
article.source: D23 — The Official Disney Fan Club

exercise.prompt: Plan a two-second animation on twos: draw 12 numbered poses, identify keyframes and in-betweens, and separate the moving subject from a reusable background.

ENGN.06.note: NASA's propulsion guide explains the compressor, combustor, turbine and nozzle, then distinguishes turbojet, turbofan, turboprop and turboshaft arrangements.

exercise.prompt: Label a turbofan cutaway and track pressure, temperature, velocity, energy transfer, and airflow through fan, compressor, combustor, turbine, bypass and nozzle.

ENGN.07.note: BYU's acoustics group explains active noise control as destructive interference produced through sensing, processing, and secondary sound sources, including practical limitations.

article.title: Active Noise Control
article.source: Brigham Young University Acoustics Research Group

exercise.prompt: Draw a feedforward ANC system with reference microphone, adaptive filter, speaker, error microphone and listener, then explain why low steady frequencies are easiest to cancel.

ENGN.08.note: WSDOT's Tacoma Narrows history explains the load path of suspension bridges and uses the 1940 failure to show why aerodynamic stability must be designed, not assumed.

deeper.title: Why the Tacoma Narrows Bridge Collapsed

exercise.prompt: Draw the load path from deck to suspenders, main cables, towers and anchorages, then add wind-induced torsion and the design features used to resist it.

ENGN.09.note: The NRC definition identifies the universal reactor functions: controlled fission, fuel, moderation where applicable, neutron economy, cooling, monitoring, control rods, shielding and protection.

exercise.prompt: Draw a thermal reactor and explain the separate jobs of fuel, moderator, coolant, control rods, pressure boundary, steam system, containment and emergency cooling.

ENGN.10.note: DOE explains batteries through chemical potential, electron flow in the external circuit, ion flow through electrolyte, charging reversibility, degradation and safety research.

article.title: DOE Explains...Batteries
article.source: U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science

exercise.prompt: Draw charge and discharge for a lithium-ion cell, showing electron and ion directions, anode, cathode, electrolyte, separator and one pathway to thermal runaway.

ENGN.11.note: GPS.gov explains the space, control and user segments, satellite time broadcasts and receiver positioning; its trilateration activity turns signal travel time into measured distance.

exercise.prompt: Use four simulated satellite positions and travel times to solve receiver location and clock offset, then list atmospheric, orbital and multipath error sources.

ENGN.12.note: OpenStax connects focal length, aperture, shutter and image formation to the sensor plane, giving the optical foundation beneath digital-camera electronics.

exercise.prompt: Photograph one subject using different focal lengths, apertures and shutter speeds, then explain changes in angle of view, perspective, depth of field, motion and sensor exposure.
